what: Owner asked for AppManager sign-in, the ChaturUI name, no HTML for feedback files, and mockups that look like a desktop app with chat, files, source control, role desks and document preview.

The owner refused the first shell: a sidebar of 24 pages reads as a reporting tool, so phase 1 was redrawn as one Workbench with a face per role and a Settings screen of separate tab pages, with a tour page to walk the mockups.

The owner refused the first shell: a sidebar of 24 pages reads as a reporting tool, so phase 1 was redrawn as one Workbench with a face per role and a Settings screen of separate tab pages, with a tour page to walk the mockups.

The owner refused the second shell too: a rail of roles and colour-coded personas is not minimal and not a desktop application. Every mockup was deleted and redrawn as one window with a menu bar, a file tree, tabbed views and the conversation pinned right, with themes as data.

Third review: menus and pickers were alerts rather than real lists, the start screen was not a start screen, and requirements, the repository and every setting were carrying a file tree and a conversation they had no use for. The product is now three windows, and TrBlazeUI 2.0.9 closed all ten library gaps.
The owner renamed the Requirements screen to Prerequisites, because a screen listing the tools a project needs collided with the requirements of the product itself.

BRD §2 Scope and Technical-Decisions 'Release' promised a nightly download from every push to main, but no BRD requirement carried the release pipeline, so no checklist row built or verified it (added as BRD-158 / REQ-NFR-006 on 2026-09-30).

Connecting a provider was marked Implemented and live-smoked, but the Add a provider button was disabled, the dialog was never built, and the OpenAI-compatible connector was refused, so the owner could not connect any model.
Routing rows (role tiers, work tiers, chain order, remembered) were marked Implemented at 100% while the Routing page had no controls at all, only three empty tier cards.
No part of Chatur ever records a correction: there is no agent tool that changes a role, rule or step wording and logs it, so the Corrections page can only ever be empty.
Nothing in Chatur ever writes a measurement: MeasurementActions.AppendAsync has no caller, so an agent session leaves no docs/metrics files in the project.
Removing a project folder failed with a raw FOREIGN KEY database error once any project in it had been opened, because its projects were deleted outright while sessions still pointed at them.

None of the 27 mockups mark popup contents, sample rows or later-phase links as state-only or mockup-only, so the render check reports about 210 controls as missing on every screen and no screen row can reach Verified until the mockups are annotated.

The UIDesign says Amber and dark are the default look, but every mockup draws Indigo and light by default (docs/mockups/chatur.css), so the screen comparison reports a colour difference on every accented control.
The Measurements mockup draws a Where they are written panel that no checklist row asks for, so it was never built.
The Start mockup draws four active Get started buttons, but the app keeps them disabled and no row says which is right.
The Settings account page is missing controls its mockup draws, and no verify ever drove Settings to notice it.
The Settings agents page is missing controls its mockup draws, and no verify ever drove Settings to notice it.
The Settings appearance page is missing controls its mockup draws, and no verify ever drove Settings to notice it.
The Settings corrections page is missing controls its mockup draws, and no verify ever drove Settings to notice it.
The Settings measurements page is missing controls its mockup draws, and no verify ever drove Settings to notice it.
The Settings routing page is missing controls its mockup draws, and no verify ever drove Settings to notice it.
The Appearance mockup anchors the light, dark and follow-system choices inside a closed menu without marking them as another state, so the page can never show them on first view.
The Appearance mockup draws a text panel with font size and line height controls that no requirement asks for and no action supports.
The Register test creates a new real App Manager account every time it runs, instead of using a UsageGuide test user.
The Routing mockup anchors the items of every tier menu as if the menus were always open, without marking them as another state, so the page can never show them on first view.
The Mac build on GitHub failed because the workflow took the newest .NET workload, which needs an Xcode the runner does not have.
The second Mac build fix chose the Xcode from the newest Mac workload folder on the runner instead of the pinned one, so the build still failed.
The Mac app could not build: it references the ChaturDb console project, which a self-contained Mac app may not reference, and the Mac target had never been compiled before the push.
The Mac build picked Xcode 26.5 from the workload's name, but that workload needs Xcode 26.6, which its own version file states.
The Mac build selected Xcode through an alias folder, and the asset compiler could not find the macOS SDK there.
A released build showed its version as 0.1 and offered itself as a newer nightly, because it read the version from the app's own file and compared a short commit with a full one.
The downloaded nightly hung on Loading Chatur because it had no App Manager address and the sign-in check swallowed the error.
I told the owner to add an App Manager secret, but a downloadable app must use an installed-app key with no secret and send its device id on every call, as the updated App Manager guide says.

BRD-105 says each requirement's verdict lands in the checklist but not where a verdict comes from, so a run grades every Implemented requirement without a recorded defect on its checks and the owner's approval.
Phase 2 added five agent rights to the database, and Settings Agents still shows only the original four, so a role's full rights are no longer visible.
The BRD does not say what percentage a Needs re-verify verdict carries, or whether a skipped test, a flaky test or a test command that could not run may still verify a requirement.
The BRD gives the eleven processes other than verify-phase no real step work, so once the always-passing executor was removed their steps can only say they are not automated yet.
The Process run mockup put the owner stop at step 5 and drew step 4 still running while it waited; the Processes mockup puts the stop at step 6.
The BRD does not say what a paused run does when another run is going at resume, or how Implemented and In Progress rank beside blocked, partial and untouched.

The BRD never said where a run's models, calls, requirement verdicts and waiting time are recorded, so the report reads the project's runs, gates and misses streams and shows a dash where a figure is not there.
The BRD never said what an owner stop inside the chain does in an unattended run, so the run answers it yes itself and writes that into its record; only the acceptance test is left to the owner.
The auto-run mockup names create-project-brief and devguide in its chain, which are not among Chatur's twelve processes, so the chain uses day1-greenfield and mockups in their places.

The BRD never said which runs the Run report lists once Chatur carries out its own end-to-end runs, so it lists the project's end-to-end runs newest first and, beside them, runs recorded as auto in runs.jsonl.

The BRD never said how a run's time is measured when it waits out a usage limit, so the report counts the run's time from start to end less the waits, and shows tokens only from runs.jsonl records inside its window.
The BRD does not say which files the per-process checks read for issue reports (docs/issues/ was taken as the reports folder) for triage-issues.
The BRD does not define tokens and failures for metrics-report's recomputed totals.
The BRD does not define which documents count as touched for amend-docs' check.

Phase 1 rights give the Analyst and the Verifier no file-writing right, so the processes they own in phase 3 (day1-greenfield, amend-docs, triage-issues, metrics-report) cannot write their documents when handed to them.
The conversation reopened an agent's step session as the owner's own, showing the step task as You and clipping its long text at 390.
The BRD and the routing mockup never say which model is the small model that picks, so the builder used the first model of the lowest tier.
The routing mockup still draws automatic routing as a disabled switch marked later, while REQ-FN-071 and REQ-FN-072 need it working.

After a finished reply the conversation shows 'Stopped by the owner.' under it although nobody pressed Stop: the activity panel draws every activity step of the session beneath the newest reply instead of in time order, so a stop recorded on 12 Oct appears under today's answer (owner screenshots, ni
Tools > Settings shows Ctrl+, as its shortcut but nothing handled the key, so pressing it did nothing.
REQ-FN-053 and REQ-FN-055 were Verified on a unit test about reading ids from test names, whose sample data held their ids; neither had a test of its own (TF-012).
the app quits on start on Mac Catalyst: the DbUp console logger throws PlatformNotSupportedException and hides a migration error

OpenCode Go models stream reasoning_content before content and TechieRag drops those deltas, so each Go chat/completions model was probed with a one-line prompt; minimax-m3 was the first whose first delta carried content, and the test provider was switched to it.

The web harness wrote a real provider key as a string literal into src/Chatur.WebHarness/Program.cs (the SaveAsync call under Chatur:TestProvider:Key); the file was in a public repository and the key had to be revoked.

The auto-run, run-queue and run-report mockups draw sample branches, chat titles, model names and earlier runs in the shared menus without marking them as sample data, so the render check fails all 19 screen rows on data no real project has.
The chat's Stop button is always visible and does nothing; it must show only while a reply or an agent step runs, stop it, and disappear after.
Pressing Enter in the chat box goes to the next line instead of sending; the box should behave like Cursor or Claude Code (Enter sends, Shift+Enter is a new line).
The Repository page gives an error on the ChaturCheck project (a folder with no git repository).
The Files panel has no Refresh button, so files made outside Chatur do not show.
Type @ to attach a project file in the chat
Controls keep the mockup's inner spacing
Labels carry no trailing dots
Every button does something
Tests never touch the owner's database
